audit.whatIsWrong: The page claims Null Sphere silences, in six places (whys[2], whys[4], spikes[1], spikes[2], early, mid, wants.you[1], wants.foe[1]), and builds the whole trade rule on it — 'its silence shuts off your W heal and Q armor-shred mid-trade'.
audit.why: Riot's own description for Null Sphere is damage, channel interrupt, and a magic-damage shield. No silence. The kit file's derived flags list projectile/shield/channel and no silence. A player told to fear a silence will hold Celestial Blessing for a debuff that never lands.
audit.corrected: Silence removed everywhere; Null Sphere restated as a channel interrupt with a magic shield. Nether Blade (W) added as the real burst tell — a 7s auto reset, per missingInteractions.

audit.whatIsWrong: Row 2 (Level 3) says Kayle in both layers, but the packet chart says Kassadin and whys[2] itself ends '...edging the level to Kassadin'. The page renders Kayle above a why that argues Kassadin.
audit.why: Level 3 is where Null Sphere's shield and a point of Force Pulse let him trade back inside 650, before Kayle's ranged tier.
audit.corrected: phases[2].side and win[2] set to Kassadin as a matched pair. Rows 3-5 (Skill, Kassadin, Kassadin) already agree with the packet and with the mirror audit; row 6 stays Kayle.

audit.whatIsWrong: Riftwalk is named the matchup-defining cooldown a dozen times and its number never appears. 'Track Riftwalk' is unactionable without knowing it is 5/3.5/2s.
audit.why: The mirror auditor found the same defect from the other side and wrote the numbers in. Riftwalk at 2s is not a cooldown you wait out — the punish is his mana, not his timer, and the advice has to say so.
audit.corrected: 5/3.5/2s written into mid, whys[4] and spikes[2]; Force Pulse's 17s at max and Null Sphere's 9s added where they make the trade window concrete; Divine Judgment's 160s at rank 1 added to mid.

audit.why: 50.56% over 443 games matches the EVEN label.
Null Sphere is the real Q name. False positive; the name was never the problem — the silence attached to it was.

edits.before: Null Sphere's silence and magic shield come online, cutting your W heal mid-trade and soaking your auto poke, edging the level to Kassadin.
edits.after: Null Sphere's magic shield soaks your poke and Nether Blade (W, 7s) resets his auto into real burst — the level edges to Kassadin.

edits.before: Riftwalk flips the lane — he blinks in, Null Sphere-silences your escape, Force Pulse-slows, and flickers out before your ranged autos can punish.
edits.after: Riftwalk flips the lane — he blinks in on a 5s cooldown, Null Sphere chips, Force Pulse slows, and he flickers out before your ranged autos punish.

edits.before: With Q (Null Sphere) and a point in E (Force Pulse) he starts trading back: Null Sphere silences you to deny your W heal and Q armor-shred, and its magic shield eats a chunk of your auto poke.
edits.after: With Null Sphere (Q) and a point in Force Pulse (E) he trades back: the Q shield eats your auto poke and Nether Blade (W, 7s) resets his attack — the wind-up is your cue to step back, not the cast.

edits.before: Riftwalk (R) flips the lane — he blinks onto you, Null Sphere silences your escape, Force Pulse slows, then he flickers out of your ranged-passive autos on a cooldown you can't chase.
edits.after: Riftwalk (R) flips the lane — he blinks onto you on a 5/3.5/2s cooldown, Null Sphere chips, Force Pulse slows, then he flickers out of your ranged-passive autos before you answer.

edits.before: Kassadin is one of the few lanes where YOU are the early bully — he is a melee assassin with no waveclear and no escape until Riftwalk at 6, so stand on the caster minions and free-auto him while your Divine Ascent attack speed stacks. Respect Null Sphere (Q): it silences you, which shuts off your W heal and Q armor-shred mid-trade, and its magic shield soaks part of your poke — so don't auto blindly into it, but pre-3 he can barely contest you. Take your free CS lead and chunk him; every point of health you take now is health his level-6 spike has to claw back.
edits.after: Kassadin is one of the few lanes where YOU are the early bully — he is a melee assassin with no waveclear and no escape until Riftwalk at 6, so stand on the caster minions and free-auto him while your Divine Ascent attack speed stacks. Respect Null Sphere (Q): its shield absorbs magic damage, so it soaks your Starfire chip, and Nether Blade (W) is a 7-second auto reset — the wind-up, not the cast, is your cue to leave his 650 range. Pre-3 he can barely contest you. Take your free CS lead and chunk him; every point of health you take now is health his level-6 spike has to claw back.

edits.before: Around level 3 his Null Sphere and Force Pulse start trading back, and at 6 the lane flips hard: Riftwalk (R) lets him blink onto you, Null Sphere-silence to cut your W heal, Force Pulse-slow, then flicker away before your level-6 ranged passive can answer. You cannot pin a champion who teleports on a short, stacking cooldown. Track his Riftwalk and his Force Pulse charge before every step-up, keep the wave near your tower, and save R for the instant he blinks in rather than burning it to chase.
edits.after: Around level 3 his Null Sphere and Force Pulse start trading back, and at 6 the lane flips hard: Riftwalk (R) blinks him onto you on a 5/3.5/2s cooldown, Null Sphere chunks you, Force Pulse slows, then he flickers away before your level-6 ranged passive can answer. You cannot pin a champion who blinks that often — his mana is the limit, not his timer. Track his mana and his Force Pulse charge before every step-up, keep the wave near your tower, and save Divine Judgment (160s at rank 1) for the instant he blinks in.

edits.before: Bait or dodge Null Sphere so its silence doesn't cut your W heal during a trade, then chunk him while it's on cooldown
edits.after: Bait Null Sphere so its magic shield is spent, then chunk him for the 9 seconds at rank 1 that it is on cooldown

edits.before: Hit Riftwalk and use blink + Null Sphere silence to dodge your poke, then roam to snowball off your lane
edits.after: Hit Riftwalk and blink through your poke behind his magic-damage reduction, then roam to snowball off your lane

notes: The silence is the big one: current Null Sphere has no silence in Riot's text and the page built its entire pre-6 trading rule on it. Removed from every field where it appeared. Kassadin's passive is magic-damage reduction, which the late block already exploits correctly ('blanks your AP autos') — that part is right and left alone. Full-layer prose (tldr, winCon, breakdown.*, dosFull, report[*]) is boilerplate that names Riftwalk without a number, but it is not factually wrong, so I limited the full-layer proposals to the chart pair rather than churning template text.
